question: what are the prereqs for organic chemistry 1 and does it have a seperate lab I have to sign up for
answer:
CHEM 211 Organic Chemistry I Lecture (4 credits) requires completion of one of: CHEM 112; or CHEM 117 General Chemistry II Lecture and CHEM 117L General Chemistry II Lab. You must also be enrolled in CHEM 211L Organic Chemistry I Lab as a corequisite. [2]

Yes—CHEM 211L is a separate 1-credit lab course, and CHEM 211L lists CHEM 211 lecture as a corequisite, so enroll in both. The lab course has a required course fee. [2][3] Student Accounts lists the CHEM 211L fee as $85.00. [7]

Sources: [2](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/CHEM211) [3](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/CHEM211L) [7](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/costinfo/course-fee/)

question: I'm a sophomore biology major planning on applying to PA school. What's the recommended order for gen chem, orgo, and physics over the next two years?
answer:
The Biology BS recommended plan is for students admitted during 2025–2026; it is a catalog sequence, not specifically a PA-school plan. [1]

General chemistry is placed in the first year: CHEM 116 and lab in fall, then CHEM 117 and lab in spring. [1]

For the plan’s second year (fall semester, total 17 credits), take CHEM 211 Organic Chemistry I and lab, or CHEM 206 Essentials of Organic Chemistry and lab. In spring, take CHEM 213 Organic Chemistry II and lab if you chose the CHEM 211 sequence; if you took CHEM 206 and lab in fall, the plan lists Studies in the Arts and Humanities instead. [1]

Physics follows in the third year: PHYS 111 and PHYS 118L in fall (total 14.5 credits), then PHYS 113 and PHYS 119L in spring (total 17 credits). [1]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SN-BS-BIOL)

question: what courses do i need for the biochemistry major vs the biology major, like which upper level classes are different
answer:
Both are Bachelor of Science majors. Shared: BIOL 111/111L, 113/113L, 332/332L and 407/407L; CHEM 117/117L; PATH 001, 002 and 003. [1][2]

Biochemistry BS: also requires CHEM 211/211L, 213/213L, 324/324L, 350/350L, 425, 430 and 446; MATH 121 and 122; PHYS 116/116L and 117/117L. [1]

Biology BS: also requires BIOL 356; PHYS 111/118L and 113/119L; one organic option (CHEM 206/206L, or CHEM 211/211L and 213/213L); one ecology course (BIOL 221 or ENSC 220); and two math courses (CMPS 147, BIOL 354 or PSYC 242, MATH 110, 121 or 122). [2]

Upper-level differences: Biochemistry requires CHEM 324, 350/350L, 425, 430 and 446, while Biology requires BIOL 356 and selects four electives. Biology electives: at least one with lab/field (BIOL 214/214L and 216/216L; 311/311L; 320; 324; 328/328L; 349; 410/410L; 420; 430; ENSC 220/220L, 320 or 417/417L) and at least one without (BIIN 350, 351; BIOL 204, 304, 335, 343, 345, 346, 347, 354, 357, 390; CHEM 425; GEOG 309; ENSC 320). [2]

Both also publish a Biology Minor. [1][2]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SN-BS-BCHM) [2](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SN-BS-BIOL)

question: Do I need to take a writing intensive course for gen ed, and do any science courses count as one?
answer:
The General Education pages list required courses and categories, but do not say that a writing-intensive course is required [4, 9]. They do not establish whether a writing-intensive science course counts toward Gen Ed [1, 4, 9]. See approved General Education courses in the College Catalog: https://catalog.ramapo.edu/college-wide-programs/gened#general-education-categories-and-courses [7].

SCIN 435 CAPSTONE FOR INTEGRATED SCIENCE STUDIES is a science course marked “Writing Intensive” [1]. It is 4 credits. Prerequisites: CRWT 102 or CRWT 102S, and one of BIOL 356, CHEM 350L, CHEM 430, ENSC 303, ENSC 417, GEOL 328, MATH 441, PHYS 242, or SCIN 295. Attributes: Capstone Course (CPST); WRITING INTENSIVE (WRIT) [1]. The catalog entry does not say that it fulfills a General Education requirement [1].

For whether a specific course applies to your Gen Ed requirements, contact the Office of the Provost: provost@ramapo.edu; (201) 684-7330; first floor of the Birch Mansion [4, 7].

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/SCIN435) [7](https://www.ramapo.edu/provost/curriculum-and-assessment/)
